previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for volume overload due to decompensated cirrhosis and portopulmonary hypertension. He presented with worsening ascites and bilateral lower extremity edema refractory to oral diuretics. During the 8-day admission, he received aggressive IV diuresis and underwent a therapeutic paracentesis, removing 7.6 liters of fluid. His weight decreased from 101 kg to 93.9 kg. A right heart catheterization was performed, showing a mean pulmonary artery pressure of 24 mmHg, indicating improved pulmonary hemodynamics. He remained on chronic medications including treprostinil, spironolactone, and rifaximin. He was discharged home with an increased dose of torsemide, instructions to monitor daily weight, and plans for weekly paracenteses and outpatient follow-up.

# Sepsis: On presentation patient was neutropenic, but quickly 
developed a WBC count to 18,000 w/ 10% bandemia. He was 
initially treated with Vancomycin and Zosyn empirically. Zosyn 
was switched to Meropenem & Doxy. Tunnelled line was pulled on

removed line and peritoneal fluid. He briefly required pressors 
during his MICU stay. The etiology of the patient's sepsis 
remained unclear. However most likely etiology was line 
infection given improvement after removal of line. ID was 
consulted who recommended putting patient on ___ to 
complete an 10 day course on ___.  ID also recommended sending 
labs for tick bone illnesses such as lyme, leptospira, anaplasma 
which were all negative. Patient completed his 10 day course of 
above antibiotics.  On day of discharge he remains afebrile, no 
leukocytosis and cultures remain negative. He will follow up in 
the ___ clinic post discharge.  
 
# Respiratory Status: Patient initially presentd with 
respiraroty distress and required BIPA support intermittently 
during the day.  His CXR showed signs of volume overload.  He 
was slowly diuresed with IV lasix with improvement in his 
respiratory symptoms. He was also continued on his remodulin 
infusion therapy for his portopulmonary hypertention through his 
PICC line.  His Sildenafil was restarted once he was 
hemodynamically stable. On day of discharge, patient 100% on 4L 
and on all of his home medications.  No SOB, dyspnea. He will 
follow up with his pulmonologist for further care. 
 
# HCV Cirrhosis: He is currently on trasnplant list and was 
closely followed by transplant team. He did require two separate 
paracentesis for comfort and to help with his breathing.  
Ascites did not reveal any signs of SBP.  He was started on 
lower dose of his diuretics in the MICU. He was continued on his 
cipro for SBP prophylasix and lactulose and rifaximine for 
history of hepatic encephalopathy. However he did not have any 
period of encephalopathy during this hospital course. Per 
transplant surgery he also had dobhoff tube placed by ___ for 
nutritional support.  He tolerated his tube feeds very well.  

# inferior NSTEMI- patient developed nonsustained Ventricular 
tachycardia while on the medical ward floor on ___.  EKG showed 
new Q waves in II,III, F, cardiac enzymes were uptrending and 
there was concern for acute myocardial infarction. He was 
transfered to the ICU as it was felt that a myocardial 
infarction would lead to serious pulmonary complications in this 
patient. He underwent LHC without complication via the right 
radial artery.  There was a distal PDA cut off that may have 
been due to embolization but no other disease present. 
Ultimately it was felt that suspicion for embolization is low- 
no further workup for endocarditis/no antibiotics. No 
interventions were made. His troponin was down trending and he 
was transferred back to the medical ward.  He will followup with 
cardiology as an outpatient.

Patients with clinical history and/or  symptoms suggestive of lyme disease should be retested in 2-3 weeks.
